primary_meaning: Jesus Christ, the Second Person of the Trinity (the Logos or Word), representing God's mind and active agent in creation.

alternatives.meaning: A poetic and literary personification of God's inherent attribute of wisdom and the divine order embedded in creation, rather than a distinct divine person.
The Holy Spirit, viewed as the breath and active presence of God in creation and revelation.
The Blessed Virgin Mary, often venerated liturgically as the Seat of Wisdom (Sedes Sapientiae) in whom the Word became flesh.

notes: In historical orthodox Christian teaching, Old Testament personifications of Wisdom (especially in Proverbs 8) were heavily utilized in early Christological debates to describe the eternal generation of the Son. While the Christological interpretation dominates historical and theological consensus, modern historical-critical scholarship commonly reads it merely as a personified divine attribute.
